The OK Movement, whose name combines those of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, has announced its withdrawal of campaign and mobilisation support for the Nigeria Democratic Congress and its presidential candidate, Obi, ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kwankwaso is Obi’s running mate in the 2027 presidential race. The movement also said it would announce its preferred political party and presidential candidate on Monday. The movement’s National Director-General, John Ughulu, announced the decision in a statement on Friday, saying the group had been informed that Obi and the NDC had decided to end their political relationship with it. Ughulu said the movement would immediately discontinue all campaign, mobilisation and operational support for the party, directing its structures at the ward, local government and state levels to withdraw from NDC activities. He said, “The National Leadership of the OK Movement has formally been made to understand that the presidential candidate of the NDC, His Excellency Peter Obi, and the party he represents have decided to discontinue their political relationship with the OK Movement. He described the movement as an independent political organisation with structures across the country, claiming that its grassroots presence and mobilisation capacity could influence the outcome of the 2027 elections. However, the NDC rejected the announcement, describing those behind it as impostors who did not represent the authentic OK Movement. He said, “There are several rogue elements masquerading as members of the OK Movement. The real OK Movement leadership and members are still supporting Peter Obi and the NDC. “Obi and the NDC will win the presidential election.” Similarly, Obi’s spokesman, Idris Zekeri, said the former Anambra State governor and his campaign organisation did not recognise Ughulu’s group as one of the support organisations backing his presidential ambition. He identified the Obidient Movement, led by Dr Moses Paul, and the Kwankwasiyya Movement, coordinated by Dr Habeeb Muhammed, as the support groups recognised by Obi’s camp. He said, “We don’t know anything about them. The real OK we know in our camp is Obidient, whose national coordinator is Dr Moses Paul and Kwankwasiyya Movement, which is led by Dr Habeeb Muhammed. “So, when you talk about another OK Movement, are we going to leave these ones for them? It is like trying to withdraw a baby from his mother. To us, this is a sheer waste of time.” The disagreement follows an earlier dispute between the OK Movement and some leaders of the NDC Presidential Campaign Council and the Obidient Movement. On November 3, the movement’s United Kingdom Coordinator, Adebayo Brown, accused the two groups of encouraging divisions among organisations supporting Obi’s 2027 ambition. Brown had urged their leaders to end what he described as unnecessary political disputes and focus on grassroots mobilisation, strengthening their structures and preparing for the elections.
